twin_rejecting.evidence: Closing the budget twice needs each series element's continuous and peak/current-limit rating; neither electrical.motor_drivers (only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage and thermal_resistance are declared, no current rating) nor electrical.battery_pack (only charge_capacity, energy_capacity, mass and supply_voltage are declared, no discharge-current or power rating) records any such rating anywhere in the design graph, before or after this revision, and sourcing it is not this revision's duty since it neither chose nor changed the driver or the battery.

Determining the rail's lowest-rated series element needs a rating for each element (driver, connector, battery) in the motor path; none of these ratings exist anywhere in the design graph (electrical.motor_drivers has no current rating at all), so the comparison cannot be made by reading, and this gap predates the revision and concerns parts the revision did not change.

Checking parts on the battery rail at both ends of the voltage window needs the cells' internal resistance to redo the sag arithmetic; no internal-resistance quantity is sourced anywhere in electrical.battery_pack or elsewhere in the design graph (unlike the chemistry, no source citation for this figure exists at all), so this input is genuinely missing and not derivable by reading, and sourcing it is not this revision's duty since the battery was not chosen or changed by it.

Comparing the motor's stall current with the driver's continuous rating, peak rating and minimum overcurrent trip needs those three driver figures; electrical.motor_drivers records none of them (only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage and thermal_resistance), and this gap predates the revision and concerns the motor driver, a part the revision did not choose or change.

Estimating junction temperature needs the driver's rDS(on) and the dissipating current; parts_sheet.json's own R4.09 row ('HS + LS FET on-resistance rDS(on)') is recorded with value null, i.e. rDS(on) has never been sourced anywhere in this design, and the motor driver itself was not chosen or changed by this revision, so this input is genuinely missing and not this revision's duty to supply.

Comparing an estimated junction temperature against the thermal shutdown minimum needs the same missing dissipation/rDS(on) input as ES-19, plus a board or ambient reference temperature, which is likewise never recorded anywhere in the design graph; the gap predates the revision and concerns the untouched motor driver.

ES-19 applies (the motor driver's dissipating current is tied to the changed motor), but no dissipation quantity is declared anywhere in the design graph for the driver (only thermal_resistance = 60.9 K/W is given), and that dissipation cannot be computed because rDS(on) was never sourced (parts_sheet R4.09 is null); this predates the revision and concerns the untouched motor driver.

mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment and control.balance_loop.torque_peak = 240 kgf*cm (derived: [R1a.13]*[R2.12] = 1.1*218.5) double-count the motor's internal 75.81:1 gear reduction, already embedded in the cited stall-torque rating R1a.13, by multiplying again by the overall ratio R2.12 that includes that same internal reduction; and electrical.motors/electrical.power/electrical.motor_drivers still use only the motor's 6V-rated stall current and the pack's nominal 7.2V, never the pack's highest voltage (~8.4V) the standards require for this exact part. Both are written by this revision (new numbers, new source citations), so the revision is not consistent with the design's own cited sources or with the rubric's ES-32/ES-14/ES-11 checks.

No continuous or peak current rating for the DRV8838 driver (parts_sheet rows R4.06, R4.07 are null) and no sourced battery discharge-current limit exist anywhere in the design graph, so the budget cannot be closed against either rating by reading.

The driver's and any connector/trace's current ratings in the motor's series path are absent from the design graph (parts_sheet R4.06-R4.08 null, no trace/connector current-rating quantities exist), so the lowest-rating-in-path comparison cannot be decided by reading.

electrical.power.supply_voltage, electrical.motor_drivers.supply_voltage and firmware.motor_output.supply_voltage are all recorded only at the nominal 7.2V; no V_max (top of window, ~8.4V for six fresh NiMH cells per electrical/standards.md §4's own worked figure) or V_min (sagged bottom) quantity is declared anywhere in the design graph for the motor branch this revision rewrote.

electrical.motors.stall_current = 1.5A is recorded at the motor's rated 6V (R1a.12) and used directly, unscaled, in electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw; electrical/standards.md §5 and skill.md step 1 give R = V_rated/I_stall = 6/1.5 = 4 ohm and I_stall,max = V_max/R, worked explicitly for this exact motor family to about 2.1A at 8.4V; the revision's written values never perform or record this scaling.

electrical.motor_drivers carries only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage and thermal_resistance; the DRV8838's continuous rating, peak rating and minimum OCP trip are not recorded anywhere in the design graph or parts sheet (R4.06-R4.08 null), so the three-way comparison cannot be made by reading for the motor this revision changed.

mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment = 240 kgf*cm and control.balance_loop.torque_peak = 240 kgf*cm (derived: [R1a.13]*[R2.12] = 1.1 kgf*cm * 218.5 = 240.35, rounds to 240, so the stated arithmetic is reproduced) double-count the motor's internal 75.81:1 gear ratio: R1a.13 is already measured at the gearmotor's geared output shaft, and R2.12 (218.5) is the overall ratio that already includes that same 75.81:1 reduction (218.5/2.88 external-only ratio = R2.02 ~= 75.9 ~= R1a.09=75.81). The physically correct torque at the wheel is R1a.13 * R2.02 (external ratio only) = 1.1*2.88 ~= 3.17 kgf*cm, not 240 kgf*cm (~23.5 N*m, implausible for a ~330g robot). This is a newly written number replacing the prior 110 kgf*cm (using the identical, equally-flawed formula pattern with the 50:1 motor's rows), so it is judged as the revision's own value and fails as a magnitude unsupported by physical sense.

electrical.power, electrical.motor_drivers and firmware.motor_output are all checked only at the nominal 7.2V pack voltage; no V_max (~8.4V) or sagged V_min quantity is declared or used anywhere in the design graph for the branch this revision rewrote.

electrical.motors.stall_current/current_draw = 1.5A is the motor's rated-6V stall current (R1a.12), used directly in electrical.power's derivation without scaling to the pack's higher voltage, matching the antipattern's exact description and the skill file's own worked example for this motor family (2.1A at 8.4V).

electrical.power/electrical.motor_drivers/firmware.motor_output (all written by this revision) are checked only at the nominal 7.2V/6V figures; electrical/standards.md §4-5 and skill.md require checking at the pack's highest voltage (~8.4V) and explicitly work this out for this exact motor (2.1A at 8.4V, exceeding the DRV8838's 1.8A peak rating and 1.9A trip). The visible, already-existing budget calculation passes at the one voltage it uses and would fail at the voltage the standards require checking, and the failing comparison uses written values.

Recorded as a blocking specification defect below.

control.balance_loop.torque_peak was rewritten to 219 kgf*cm via source '[R1.07] * [R2.11] * [R2.26]' (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; journal.jsonl rev 30, replacing rev 20's 110 kgf*cm). R1.07 (0.74 kgf*cm, https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs) is the Pololu 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor's stall torque measured at the gearbox OUTPUT shaft, i.e. already reduced by the motor's own internal ~51.45:1 gear ratio (R1.12). R2.11 (148.3, https://www.pololu.com/file/0J1266/balboa-kit-gear-ratio-chart.pdf) is explicitly the COMBINED internal*external gear ratio for '50:1 gearmotor with 49:17 external gearbox' (51.45*2.88 ~= 148.2). Multiplying R1.07 by R2.11 therefore reapplies the internal 51.45:1 reduction a second time, inflating torque by roughly 51x; a physically consistent combined torque (gearmotor output torque * external-only ratio R2.02=2.88, doubled for two drivetrains via R2.26 or R1.25) would be on the order of 4.3 kgf*cm. The written value of 219 kgf*cm (~21.5 N*m) for a 330 g robot (the node's own 'mass' quantity) is implausible by roughly two orders of magnitude, so the revision is not consistent with the parts sheet's own row definitions or with sound physical reasoning for the design it changes.
